qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Deep enterprise integration relationships, multi-year managed services contracts, and trusted C-suite advisory status embed Accenture across 90+ of the Fortune Global 100, supporting high asset turnover and multi-decade ROIC > 25%.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Macrotrend #1 (Automation & Cognitive Tech / AI Disruption) poses an unhedged terminal headwind to Accenture's billable-hour IT consulting and headcount-intensive systems integration model. Autonomous coding agents, automated migration toolchains, and AI-driven synthetic integration structurally compress the billable hours and personnel required for enterprise digital transformations. Despite short-term GenAI consulting bookings ($5.9B in FY25), productivity deflation in its 750,000+ delivery workforce caps competitive advantage period at 5 years. Downstream gates bypassed per waterfall.
qualitative.evidence: Accenture demonstrates strong historical capital efficiency with a 10-year median ROIC of 26.8% and owner FCF conversion exceeding 100%. In FY24, revenue was $64.9B with adjusted operating margin of 15.5% and FCF of $8.6B. FY25 revenue reached $69.7B with adjusted operating margin of 15.6%, FCF of $10.9B, and total debt of $5.08B offset by $11.48B in cash. While entrenched across 90+ Fortune Global 100 clients, Mauboussin-Callahan empirical persistence research places IT Services in Tier 3 (10-15Y baseline CAP). Under Step 2 inside view, Macrotrend #1 (AI Disruption) imposes a severe haircut: generative AI agents and automated code generation commoditize routine IT implementation, eroding headcount-based billing volume and client willingness to pay standard consulting billing rates over a multi-decade horizon.
